chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'azi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalesi, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever performs the Hajj pilgrimage twenty times, he will not see the Fire of Hell, nor will he hear its roaring nor its sighing.

key_terms.عِشْرِينَ حَجَّةً: twenty times (referring to twenty Hajj pilgrimages)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing the Hajj pilgrimage twenty times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to highlight the immense spiritual merit of repeated Hajj, a practice often associated with the 'Hajj al-Tamattu'' or voluntary pilgrimages performed by the pious. The description of not hearing its 'breath' (shahiq) and 'sigh' (zafir) draws on poetic imagery to signify a total, absolute deliverance from the torments of Hellfire, reinforcing the concept of divine mercy through sustained devotion.
